Replacing a conv by a skip discards learnable capacity, which is worse than replacing weaker ops.
Adding any op to a severed output edge restores a path, which gains more than swapping one op for pooling.

Removing the conv on the inter-node edge loses more than removing a weak op, because it is the only conv linking the two paths.

The edge 1 to node 2 path is cut off from the output when edge 5 is none, so the edit has little effect.
A strong direct conv already supplies capacity to the output, so extra conv on edge 4 is partly redundant.
The direct conv on edge 3 makes a parallel conv on edge 5 more redundant, so the marginal gain is smaller.
